own_solution.law: kinetic theory of an ideal gas: v_rms = sqrt(3 R T / M)
assumptions: ideal gas (stated) in thermal equilibrium at T = 300 K

notes: Base: v_rms = sqrt(3*8.314*300/0.004) = sqrt(1,870,650) = 1367.7 m/s. At 400 K: sqrt(2,494,200) = 1579.3 m/s. TA729/T60E8 (2 mol, same number and unit, consistent variants): n enters the energy relation (1/2) n M v_rms^2 = (3/2) n R T and cancels, so C. T58F9 (100 K up and back down) and its numeral-free counterpart T62B1: the temperature change acts on the sample but returns, so C. T0B42/T4B0A: heating a separate sample in another flask, D. T84A9 (held at +100 K during measurement) R. T2DEA says the sample is warmed by 100 K before measurement without saying whether it is held; the natural reading is that it is at 400 K when measured (R), but it is slightly less explicit than T84A9. T84A9, T58F9, T0B42 and T2DEA all state 100 K consistently.
